rationale: Says the field has moved to provable security and seamless open-model deployment 'without API access or fine-tuning', overstating how mature cryptographic and learning-based schemes are.
Transition sentence pointing back to limitations claimed in 3.1.

Close to Christ et al.'s computationally undetectable watermark, but 'statistically identical' and 'rejection sampling' do not match that construction (pseudorandom sampling, computational indistinguishability).
Continues describing [64] with added details. [64] trains a detector and tunes the LLM with PPO; it has no encoder that updates logits and no KL-from-green-list reward.
Presents speculative modulation signals (factual claim density, safety-criticality thresholds) as established practice.
Claims a formal risk-guided objective and that sub-percentage probability shifts weaken guardrails, without support.
Signpost only.
Grand claim that risk modeling 'transcends' into a general architecture for verifiable responsible generation.
Roadmap that says certified guarantees 'formalize robustness promises' of WaterMax and VLA-Mark, a link no source makes.
States as settled that these layers are 'essential prerequisites' and mutually reinforcing.
Reasserts a 'catastrophic failure' result attributed to BanglaLorica, which no cited source supports.
Broad statement that black-box watermarking has moved beyond synonym insertion.
Framing link between black-box methods and earlier subsections.
Claims only randomized smoothing and ECC give formal robustness certificates, ignoring other provable schemes (e.g., [31] distortion-free bounds).
Roadmap of four evaluation dimensions.
Intrinsic weight-space fingerprinting is indeed training-free and passive by definition.
Matches [22]: functionally equivalent copies via permutation/scaling, identical outputs, stealthy. Here it is left uncited.
Speculative future direction stated as a possibility ('may yield').
Characterizes backdoor watermarking as key-dependent fine-tuning; acceptable framing.
Says backdoor watermarks persist across EaaS, API wrappers and quantized edge variants at zero runtime cost, which is not established in general.
Signpost only.
Continues describing EmbMarker [23] with an added '<0.2% degradation on GLUE' figure that is not in the abstract; EmbMarker evaluates SST2, MIND, AG News and Enron Spam.
Continues describing [79]: multi-stage MIT-style fingerprinting and resistance to guessing are in the abstract, but 'semantic obfuscation' and '98.7% robustness' are added details.
Claims backdoor imprinting is 'more robust than behavior-space signatures' with no comparative evidence.
Reasonable statement of key-leakage and adaptive fine-tuning threats.
Transition contrasting backdoor and behavior-space methods.
Framing definition of behavior-space fingerprinting.
Contrastive framing of the three paradigms.
Asserts a 'stable cross-layer geometry of neuron activation density' as an established fingerprinting basis without support.
Says intermediate activations are available via API providers, which commercial APIs generally do not expose.
Presents a speculative 'dynamic, context-sensitive' parameter-watermark paradigm as an observed shift.
Lists motivating imperatives; framing.
Broad trend statement about embedding watermarks within inference.
Claims a maturation toward watermarks that interoperate from confidential-computing enclaves to multimodal pipelines, which is unsupported.
Says model-centric security is grounded in the 'cryptographic hardness of parameter inversion', a property no surveyed scheme establishes.
Short transition claim.
Reasonable caveat that guarantees assume white-box access and static models.
Future-work proposal.
